statement: One line holds n (at least 2). Print every prime from 2 to n in increasing order, space-separated, using the sieve of Eratosthenes: an array of flags, everything from 2 presumed prime, and each surviving prime p striking out its multiples starting at p squared - smaller multiples of p fell earlier, to smaller primes. The outer loop needs to run only while p squared stays within n; everything still standing beyond that point is proven prime.

example.why: 2 strikes 4, 6, 8, 10; then 3 strikes 9; the four survivors are the primes.

hint: Two loops over flags - the striking starts at p squared, and 0 and 1 are excused by hand.
mistake: Running trial division per number; correct, but the sieve shares the work and runs in a blink at a million.
